summary.one_line: A Jaipur-registered, Mumbai-assembled brand of China-sourced Wi-Fi access points and switches with fast-improving reported profits, but extreme customer concentration, a related-party export channel, weak cash conversion and an issue that mostly funds working capital and a small, unstarted factory: avoid.
bull_points: Restated revenue from operations grew from Rs 22.00 cr (FY24) to Rs 28.01 cr (FY25) and Rs 39.09 cr (FY26), and PAT from Rs 1.13 cr to Rs 6.08 cr (S5, S6).
EBITDA margin expanded from 12.16% in FY24 to 24.06% in FY26 and 25.15% in H1 FY27 (six months to 30 Sep 2026) (S5).
Debt-to-equity fell from 2.45x in FY24 to 0.38x in FY26 as net worth rose from Rs 4.30 cr to Rs 12.91 cr (S5, S2).
Products carry TEC MTCTE certification for LAN switches and Wi-Fi access points, and the company has in-house firmware customisation and its own AirproCloud management platform (S6, S5).
Promoters are still locked in after listing: 20% of post-issue capital for three years, and the rest of their holding half for one year and half for two (S5).
bear_points: Top 10 customers were 98.46% of H1 FY27 revenue (92.64% in FY26). One national distributor alone was 36.79% (S5, S6).
Imports were 71% of purchases in H1 FY27, all of them from China. Most suppliers have no long-term agreement (S5).
Related-party transactions were 30.01% of H1 FY27 revenue. Sales to Airpro FZ-LLC alone were Rs 4.55 cr, or 23.57% of revenue, and exports (23.65%) flow mainly through related-party sales (S5).

Receivable days were 159 at 30 Sep 2026 (Rs 16.85 cr of receivables against Rs 19.32 cr of half-year revenue). Operating cash flow was negative Rs 0.52 cr in H1 FY27 while borrowings rose to Rs 8.15 cr (S5).
Rs 13.00 cr of the Rs 24.91 cr net proceeds goes to working capital. The Jaipur factory has no machinery orders placed and has not started operations (S5).
Promoters and promoter-group members sell 6.80 lakh shares (Rs 6.73 cr) in the OFS. The disclosed acquisition costs are Rs 1.79 to Rs 2.42 per share, against a Rs 99 offer price (S2, S5).
watch_points: Who owns and controls Airpro FZ-LLC, and on what pricing terms it buys, was not confirmed in any source opened (S5).
Whether FY26-level margins (24% EBITDA) hold once related-party export sales and the national distributor are excluded (S5).
Machinery orders and building completion at Jaipur, which needs 6-8 months of construction after funding (S5).
Trend in receivables and operating cash flow in the H2 FY27 numbers after listing (S5).
Final category-wise subscription by the 1 Dec 2026 close. Day-1 midday demand was only about 0.30x (S12, S13).

reasoning: The fresh money mostly does not build anything durable. Of Rs 24.91 cr of net proceeds, Rs 13.00 cr (52%) goes to working capital and Rs 4.34 cr to general corporate purposes. Only Rs 7.57 cr goes to land, building and machinery for a Jaipur factory with no orders placed. Issue expenses of Rs 4.00 cr take about 14% of the fresh issue (S2, S5).

There is no real moat. The company assembles and re-brands networking hardware built from China-sourced finished goods, chipsets and modules (100% of imports from China). It competes with TP-Link, Cisco, HPE and the listed D-Link India, whose FY26 standalone revenue of about Rs 1,559 cr is roughly 40x Airpro's (S5, S17, S18).
The revenue base is fragile. The top customer is 36.87% and the top 10 are 98.46% of H1 FY27 revenue, so losing a single distributor could take away more than a third of sales (S5).

Governance questions sit right at the core of the growth story. About 30% of H1 FY27 revenue was related-party transactions, including 23.57% of revenue sold to Airpro FZ-LLC. The sharp margin jump (EBITDA margin from 15.28% in FY25 to 24.06% in FY26) came in the years just before the IPO, and we could not independently check either (S5).

Reported profit is not turning into cash. Receivable days are 159, H1 FY27 operating cash flow was negative and borrowings rose from Rs 4.97 cr to Rs 8.15 cr in six months, all while the company reported Rs 3.18 cr of PAT (S5, S2).

Promoters are cashing out part of their stake at about 40-55x their disclosed cost per share through the OFS. They also have unrelated ventures in surety, financial advisory and realty, which raises a question about how much attention they will give this business (S5, S14).

blocks.text: Airpro Technology India was incorporated in Rajasthan on 17 February 2014 as a private company and became a public limited company on 28 April 2025 (S7, S14). It designs, assembles, distributes and services wired and wireless networking equipment under its own AIRPRO brand. The range covers wireless access points, wireless LAN controllers, gateways, Ethernet switches, outdoor wireless bridges, 4G/5G customer-premises equipment (CPE), fibre-access equipment and industrial PoE switches (S2, S5, S6). It also offers AirproCloud, a cloud platform for remote configuration and monitoring that currently runs on Android devices, plus customised firmware for some white-label products (S2, S5).

In practice the product line is narrow. In the six months to 30 September 2026, wireless access points were 57.97% of revenue and Ethernet switches 33.95%. The two together make up 91.92% of sales. Other products and installation were 8.08%, and services were a negligible 0.02% (S5). This is a hardware box business. The cloud software and service lines are not yet meaningful revenue earners.

blocks.caption: Revenue mix by product, H1 FY27 (six months to 30 Sep 2026)

blocks.text: In management's own interview from GITEX Dubai (Nov 2024), the pitch is Wi-Fi 6/Wi-Fi 7 access points for high-density sites such as campuses, outdoor APs with a 200-300 m range, industrial PoE switches and point-to-point links for CCTV, with customers able to customise the hardware's appearance (S19). This is a solid mid-market feature set, but it is not technology that competitors cannot match.

subsections.title: How revenue is earned: channels, customers and geography

blocks.text: Airpro sells almost entirely B2B, through a distributor-led channel: a national distributor, regional distributors, system integrators and online channel partners. These in turn serve enterprises, education, hospitality, healthcare and government end-users (S5, S6). One listing aggregator puts the network at 47 dealers and distributors in India and overseas (S13); we could not verify this against the prospectus. A single national distributor accounted for 36.79% of H1 FY27 revenue, and system integrators contributed 33.77% of FY26 revenue (S5).

Customer concentration is extreme and rising. The largest customer was 36.87% of H1 FY27 revenue, the top three 72.84%, the top five 88.97% and the top ten 98.46%. The top-ten share was 82.76% in FY25 and 92.64% in FY26 (S5). In effect, Airpro's revenue is a handful of channel relationships, not a broad customer base.

blocks.caption: Customer concentration (share of revenue from operations)

blocks.text: By geography, the Western region contributed 46.14% and the Southern region 28.68% of H1 FY27 revenue, with Maharashtra alone at 32.82% (S5). Exports were 23.65%, sold mainly through related-party sales (S5). The export markets named are the UAE, Thailand, Nepal and Vietnam (S6).

The export book and the related-party book largely overlap: sales to Airpro FZ-LLC were 23.57% of H1 FY27 revenue, almost exactly the 23.65% export share (S5). Nearly a quarter of revenue is therefore not an arm's-length test of end-market demand.

subsections.title: Operations and supply chain, end to end

blocks.text: The supply chain is import-first. Key inputs are finished goods, semiconductor chipsets, networking modules, PCB assemblies, antennas and other electronic components. Imports were 71.00% of total purchases in H1 FY27, and China supplied 100% of imports in every period presented (S5). The top ten suppliers were 79.18% of H1 FY27 purchases, and most suppliers and contract manufacturers have no long-term agreements (S5). Because the inventory includes imported finished goods, part of what is sold is likely bought complete and re-branded.

Current operations are small. Assembly and testing of access points happens at a facility in Goregaon East, Mumbai, with after-sales service centres in Jaipur and Mumbai (S6, S10). One aggregator cites an assembly capacity of 24,000 units a year (S13); we could not verify this against the prospectus. The company had 39 permanent employees on 30 September 2026 (S2, S6). The registered office is in Jaipur and the corporate office in Mumbai (S6, S14).

The IPO plan is to add a manufacturing facility in Jaipur on land the company is part-way through paying for. That facility had not begun commercial operations at the prospectus date, no orders had been placed for its plant and machinery, and the building is expected to take six to eight months to construct (S5). Production capacity figures for the new plant are not disclosed in the summaries we could access (S5).

items: Source components and finished units, 100% of imports from China (S5)
Assemble, test and load firmware in Mumbai (S6, S10)
Sell through a national distributor, regional distributors, system integrators and online partners (S5)
Support: warranties of up to three years, with warranty cost about 0.35% of revenue (S5)
Planned: move part of assembly and manufacturing to a new Jaipur factory (S5)

blocks.text: Estimates of Airpro's market vary widely with scope. TechSci Research values the India enterprise network (LAN) equipment market at USD 3.60 bn in 2024, rising to USD 6.83 bn by 2030 at an 11.10% CAGR, driven by digital transformation, cloud/IoT adoption, Digital India and Smart Cities programmes, and hybrid work (S16). IMARC uses a narrower scope and puts the same market at USD 930.9 mn in 2025 (S21), while Statista estimates India enterprise network infrastructure revenue at USD 1.39 bn in 2024 (S22).

IDC's quarterly tracker gives a sense of the segments Airpro actually sells into. In 2Q22, India Ethernet switch vendor revenue was USD 157 mn a quarter (+6.4% YoY) and WLAN USD 59.9 mn (+19.2%), with enterprise WLAN growing 29.4% (S17). The data is dated, but it shows WLAN is the faster-growing segment and is still small in absolute terms. IDC itself expected only single-digit CAGRs for switches, routers and WLAN over 2021-2026 (S17).

blocks.caption: Third-party market estimates (scopes differ, not directly comparable)

blocks.text: Even on the smallest estimate (USD 930.9 mn), Airpro's FY26 revenue of Rs 39.09 cr is a fraction of one percent of the market (S5, S21). Growth for Airpro depends on winning share, not on the market expanding.

Global vendors dominate the market. In IDC's India data, Cisco held 51.1% of Ethernet switching, followed by Arista and HPE. In WLAN overall, TP-Link led with 28.6%; in enterprise WLAN, Cisco led with 28.2% and HPE followed at 12.5% (S17). TechSci lists Cisco, Huawei, Juniper, Dell, IBM, Broadcom, Fortinet and Arista as the major players (S16).

The prospectus peer set is D-Link (India) and Black Box (S4, S6). D-Link India, the closest listed comparable because networking products are its single reportable segment, reported FY26 standalone revenue from operations of about Rs 1,559 cr (S18, S6). That is about 40 times Airpro's Rs 39.09 cr (S5). Airpro also competes with many unlisted Indian and Chinese brands selling white-label Wi-Fi gear through the same distributor and system-integrator channels. We found no source that sizes this unbranded segment.

items: Global enterprise vendors: Cisco, HPE (Aruba), Arista, Juniper, Huawei, Fortinet (S16, S17)
Volume SMB and consumer brands: TP-Link, the WLAN volume leader in IDC data (S17)
Listed Indian peers named in the prospectus: D-Link (India), Black Box (S4, S6)
Implicit: other importers and re-branders selling into system integrators (not sized in any source found)

blocks.text: We do not find a genuine moat. Airpro claims customised configurations, in-house firmware, a diversified portfolio, an established distribution network and TEC MTCTE certifications (S6). MTCTE is a mandatory telecom-equipment certification for selling in India. It is a compliance cost that every vendor in the market, including Cisco, TP-Link and D-Link, must also meet, so it is not a barrier that protects Airpro.

Neither the prospectus summaries nor the aggregators cite any import-substitution position, market-share claim, sole-supplier status or proprietary silicon (S5, S6). The hardware is built from China-sourced chipsets and modules (S5). Firmware customisation and a cloud dashboard are standard features among white-label networking vendors. The customer-concentration data also suggests the business rests on a few distributor relationships, not on end-user brand pull (S5).

No real moat. Airpro is a small brand-owner and assembler of imported networking hardware in a market led by global vendors. Its competitive position rests on channel relationships and price, both of which can be lost.

Sources: S5, S6 and S2, which agree on all overlapping figures. Revenue from operations grew 27.3% in FY25 and 39.6% in FY26 (our calculation from S5). For context, the company reported total income of Rs 21.15 cr and PAT of Rs 0.75 cr in FY23 (S7). Revenue therefore barely moved between FY23 and FY24 before accelerating in the two years before the IPO.

Profit grew much faster than sales. PAT rose 5.4x from FY24 to FY26 while revenue rose 1.8x, because EBITDA margin doubled from 12.16% to 24.06% (S5). The prospectus summaries we read do not explain the margin change: no change in pricing, product mix, or the share of higher-margin related-party export sales is broken out (S5). For a re-brander of imported hardware, a 24-25% EBITDA margin is unusually high, and investors should not assume it is permanent.

H1 FY27 revenue of Rs 19.32 cr is about flat on an annualised basis against FY26's Rs 39.09 cr (S5). The prospectus summary notes that partial-period data cannot confirm full-year results (S5). So growth may already be slowing, although the second half could be seasonally stronger.

subsections.title: Balance sheet, working capital and cash flow

blocks.caption: Balance sheet and cash flow (Rs crore)

blocks.text: Sources: S2, S5, S6. Leverage improved sharply in FY26, when operating cash flow of Rs 7.50 cr was used to cut borrowings to Rs 4.97 cr (S5, S6). In the first half of FY27 the trend reversed. Operating cash flow was negative Rs 0.52 cr despite Rs 3.18 cr of PAT, and borrowings rose to Rs 8.15 cr (Rs 2.38 cr long-term and Rs 5.77 cr short-term), leaving cash of only about Rs 7.53 lakh at 30 September 2026 (S5). Borrowings were reported at Rs 5.04 cr on 31 October 2026, a different date and measure (S5).

Working capital is the real issue. At 30 September 2026, inventory was Rs 11.22 cr and trade receivables Rs 16.85 cr, against Rs 19.32 cr of half-year revenue; receivable days were 159 (S5). Receivables plus inventory (Rs 28.07 cr) make up most of the Rs 32.65 cr balance sheet (our calculation from S2, S5). In other words, the business carries more than five months of sales as unpaid bills, mostly from a few distributors. This also explains why Rs 13 cr of the IPO goes to working capital (S5).

Debt is mainly an ICICI Bank cash-credit facility at floating rates, secured on stock, receivables, current assets and specified property, and personally guaranteed by directors and KMPs (S5). Registry data shows three ICICI Bank charges totalling about Rs 7.9 cr, the latest created or modified on 16 July 2026 (S14). No material financial covenants are disclosed (S5).

Cash flow does not match profit. Over FY24 to H1 FY27, cumulative operating cash flow (about Rs 9.07 cr) trails cumulative PAT (Rs 12.68 cr), and the most recent half-year turned cash-negative while receivable days reached 159 (our calculation from S5).

subsections.title: Does the trend support the growth story?

blocks.text: Partly. The top line has genuinely grown at 27-40% a year for two years and the balance sheet has de-levered (S5). Against that, the growth came with a rising top-ten customer share (82.76% to 98.46%), a related-party export channel worth about a quarter of revenue, and receivables piling up faster than cash comes in (S5). Growth driven by channel stuffing, related-party sales or a single distributor would look much the same in the reported numbers. The data available to us cannot rule this out.

Reserves and surplus fell from Rs 4.70 cr (FY25) to Rs 3.33 cr (FY26) while net worth almost doubled to Rs 12.91 cr (S2). Paid-up capital is about Rs 9.58 cr (S14). This pattern is consistent with reserves being converted into share capital (such as a bonus issue) ahead of the IPO. We could not confirm the exact capital history from the prospectus. It explains why the promoters' per-share acquisition costs are so low (S5).

There is no dividend history (S5), and the IPO itself will raise net worth by roughly Rs 24.91 cr of net fresh capital (S5). That makes FY26's 47-62% return ratios unrepeatable on the enlarged equity base unless profit grows sharply.

sections.title: Issue details and objects of the issue

subsections.title: Issue structure: fresh issue vs OFS

blocks.caption: Offer structure (fixed price Rs 99, face value Rs 10, NSE Emerge)

blocks.text: Sources: S2, S3, S5. The issue opens 27 November and closes 1 December 2026. Allotment is on 2 December, refunds and demat credit on 3 December, and listing is tentatively on 4 December 2026 on NSE SME/Emerge (S2, S7). The lot size is 1,200 shares, and the minimum application is two lots, or 2,400 shares worth Rs 2,37,600 (S2, S3). Shares rise from 95,81,970 before the issue to 1,25,01,970 after it (S2). Horizon Management is the lead manager, MUFG Intime the registrar (S2), and Choice Equity Broking the market maker (S9). Because this is a fixed-price SME issue, there is no QIB or anchor portion (S2, S8).

About 19% of the issue (Rs 6.73 cr) is OFS money that goes to the promoter family, not to the company (S2). The disclosed average acquisition cost is Rs 2.42 per share for Deepak Jain and Rs 1.79 for Roopali Bhansali, against the Rs 99 offer price (S5).

subsections.title: Objects of the fresh issue, in full

blocks.caption: Use of fresh-issue proceeds (Rs crore)
rows: Rs 8.00 cr FY27, Rs 5.00 cr FY28
Purchase of machinery for manufacturing facility
Balance payment for land, Jaipur factory

blocks.text: Sources: S2, S5. Shares of net proceeds are our calculation. Only Rs 7.57 cr (about 30% of net proceeds) goes to physical capacity at Jaipur. The prospectus summary describes the factory building at about Rs 4.99 cr and a total project cost of Rs 7.12 cr, slightly different from the Rs 4.97 cr allocated (S5). No orders for plant and machinery had been placed, and the objects have not been appraised by any bank or independent agency (S5). Any shortfall would be funded from internal accruals, borrowings or unsecured loans, and no alternative financing has been identified (S5).

General corporate purposes of Rs 4.34 cr are about 15% of the gross fresh issue (our calculation from S2), roughly at the regulatory ceiling, so this money has almost no stated purpose. Issue expenses of Rs 4.00 cr are about 13.8% of the fresh issue, with underwriting at Rs 1.36 cr and lead-manager fees at Rs 0.40 cr (S2). That is high even by SME standards.

In plain terms, more than half the money funds receivables and inventory, which the business has so far struggled to turn into cash. The 'manufacturing' story amounts to a Rs 2 cr machinery budget for a factory that is not yet built (S5).

The promoters are Deepak Jain, Rajesh Hasmukh Vakharia, Pankaj Bhansali and Roopali Bhansali (S2, S5). Deepak Jain (Managing Director, 47) and Rajesh Vakharia (Whole-time Director, 57) have been with the company since incorporation and each has more than 12 years of IT experience (S5, S13). Pankaj Bhansali (Non-Executive Director, 50) is described as a Chartered Accountant with over 13 years in finance, and Roopali Bhansali (45) is a Non-Executive Director (S5, S13). The other directors on the registry are Manish Kawadia and Mantra Nath Jha, both appointed in roughly the last year, and the CFO is Manoj Navratanmal Jain (S14).

blocks.caption: Pre-issue promoter and promoter-group shareholding (as reported by one aggregator)

blocks.text: Source: S13. Pre-issue promoter and group holding is reported at 95.00% (S2, S8) or 95.33% (S13). Post-issue holding varies by source: 68.12% (S5, S8) or 69.81% (S2). The operating promoter, Deepak Jain, owns the largest block. The Bhansali family, whose main roles are non-executive, together owns around half the company (S13).

Track record. Registry records show Deepak Jain was a director of Netstream Networks Pvt Ltd from May 2013 to June 2025 and of Telvass Systems Pvt Ltd from 2014 to 2017 (S15). Netstream Networks shares two directors with Airpro (S14). Its business is not described in any source we opened, and given the similar name it is worth checking for overlap. Ventures linked to the promoter group include Anjali Lifestyle, Eqaro Surety, Arth Capital Advisors, Mehta Financial Services, Mangaldeep Infratech LLP and Mehta Energy LLP (S5). Pankaj Bhansali has been a director of Eqaro Surety since its incorporation in November 2019 (S20). So the Bhansali side has interests mainly in finance, surety and realty, not networking.

This is not a routine RPT section. Related-party transactions were Rs 6.32 cr in H1 FY27, or 30.01% of revenue (S5). The largest item is product sales to Airpro FZ-LLC of Rs 4.55 cr, or 23.57% of revenue, and the prospectus summary says exports (23.65% of revenue) were mainly related-party sales (S5). The name suggests a UAE free-zone entity. We could not confirm who owns it from any source we opened, and web and registry searches found no public record (S5).

Promoters have also personally guaranteed the company's banking facilities and lent it unsecured loans. The prospectus summary does not give a single aggregate figure for those loans (S5). Personal guarantees are normal for an SME of this size. The size and nature of the export RPT is not.

items: Rs 4.55 cr of sales to Airpro FZ-LLC in H1 FY27, 23.57% of revenue (S5)
Total RPTs of Rs 6.32 cr, 30.01% of H1 FY27 revenue (S5)
Unsecured loans from promoters (amount not aggregated) and personal guarantees on ICICI Bank facilities (S5)
Common directorship with Netstream Networks Pvt Ltd, an entity with a similar name (S14, S15)

blocks.text: Nearly a quarter of revenue goes to a related overseas entity whose ownership and on-sale terms are not visible to us. Investors cannot tell whether this is genuine end demand or sales booked to a related company, and it overlaps with the period of sharp margin expansion (S5).

Disclosed litigation is small in value. The company has three proceedings (two tax, one statutory/regulatory) totalling Rs 0.76 lakh. Promoters and directors face three proceedings (one criminal, two tax) totalling Rs 30.95 lakh, and there are none against KMPs. The materiality threshold is Rs 15.84 lakh (S5). The nature of the criminal matter against a promoter or director is not described in the summaries we accessed.

Separately, an NCLT matter involving Reliance Communications required Airpro to refund Rs 48.00 lakh, which the company says it has paid in full (S5). The registry shows the company active, with its last AGM on 30 September 2026 and no flagged compliance risks (S14). We found no reports of SEBI or exchange action.

Lock-in: the promoters' minimum contribution of 20% of post-issue capital (25,00,394 shares) is locked in for three years. The rest of the promoter holding is locked in half for one year and half for two years from allotment (S5). We could not confirm lock-in terms for any non-promoter pre-IPO shareholders.

items: Distributor and customer concentration: one national distributor was 36.79% of H1 FY27 revenue and the top 10 customers 98.46%. Losing or downsizing one relationship could cut revenue by a third (S5, S8).

China supply dependence: 71% of purchases are imported and 100% of imports come from China, with no long-term supply agreements. Tariffs, trusted-source or anti-dumping rules, chip shortages or forex moves would hit costs directly (S5, S6).
Product concentration: access points and switches are 91.92% of revenue, both commoditising hardware categories where global vendors set prices (S5, S17).
Regional concentration: Maharashtra alone is 32.82% of revenue and the West and South together about 75% (S5).

blocks.text: These risks reinforce each other. A small importer selling through a few distributors has little pricing power on either side. If the national distributor demands better terms or a supplier raises prices, the margin gains of FY26 could reverse quickly (S5).
The concentration risk is not a boilerplate warning here: a 98.46% top-ten share is about as concentrated as revenue can get (S5).

items: Related-party revenue: 23.57% of H1 FY27 revenue was sold to Airpro FZ-LLC and total RPTs were 30.01% of revenue (S5).
Working capital and credit risk: 159 receivable days, negative H1 FY27 operating cash flow and rising short-term debt, all exposed to a few counterparties (S5, S6).
Execution risk at Jaipur: the factory is unbuilt, no machinery has been ordered, the objects are unappraised and no alternative funding has been identified for any shortfall (S5).
Promoter-side litigation: one criminal and two tax proceedings against promoters/directors (Rs 30.95 lakh), plus the Rs 48 lakh NCLT refund linked to Reliance Communications (S5).

blocks.text: SME listing risks also apply. Trading is thin, the minimum lot is about Rs 2.4 lakh, and there is no QIB or anchor price discovery in a fixed-price issue (S2, S10). Promoter lock-ins (three years on 20% of capital, one to two years on the rest) limit immediate promoter selling, but they end sooner than the cleanest mainboard structures (S5).
Floating-rate debt secured on stock and receivables means a slowdown in collections and higher interest rates would hurt profit at the same time (S5).

We found no concrete forward guidance on revenue, margin or capacity from management in the prospectus summaries or in any post-filing interview. The prospectus analysis we accessed explicitly notes there are no forward-looking projections (S5). The closest thing to stated strategy is the objects of the issue: start in-house manufacturing in Jaipur and fund a larger working-capital base to support sales growth (S5).

In a November 2024 interview at GITEX Dubai, founder Deepak Jain spoke of expanding presence in the market. He highlighted Wi-Fi 6/7 access points, industrial PoE switches and cloud management for education, hospitality, transportation, logistics and smart-city customers, and mentioned inquiries from Oman, Qatar and Bahrain (S19). These are aspirations, not targets. The Gulf focus fits the related-party export channel through Airpro FZ-LLC (S5).

Management has given no numbers to hold it to. Any outlook beyond 'more Wi-Fi boxes through more channels, eventually partly made in Jaipur' would be our own inference from history, not something the company has said.

subsections.title: Milestones that would change the view

items: Placement of machinery orders and completion of the Jaipur building within the stated 6-8 months (S5).
Disclosure of Airpro FZ-LLC's ownership and a falling related-party share of revenue (S5).
Receivable days falling meaningfully below 159 and positive operating cash flow across full FY27 (S5).
Top-ten customer share falling from about 98% as new channels are added (S5).
FY27 full-year revenue actually growing beyond the roughly flat annualised H1 run-rate (S5).

blocks.text: Until at least two of these happen, the investment case rests on trusting reported numbers that depend heavily on related parties and a few distributors. The industry tailwind of roughly 11% CAGR for India LAN equipment (S16) helps everyone in the market equally and does not by itself favour Airpro.

This report is written on day 1 of a five-day issue, so the figures below are partial midday snapshots and say nothing reliable about final demand. At about 12:09 PM IST on 27 November 2026 the issue was subscribed 0.30x overall, with the individual/retail portion at 0.38x and NII at 0.23x (S13). A separate tracker showed 0.3x overall at 12:00 PM (S12) and another 0.32x (S11). Some pages had not yet published any day-1 numbers (S9).
There are no anchor investors because this is a fixed-price SME issue (S8). Choice Equity Broking is the market maker for 1,80,000 shares (S9, S2).

Grey market premium (unofficial, unregulated, not an investment signal): reported at Rs 3 on 27 Nov 2026, about 3% over the Rs 99 price, after ranging between Rs 0 and Rs 4 over 24-26 Nov (S11, S13). This small, unstable premium does not change our view in either direction.

method: We located the Draft Prospectus dated 29 June 2026 on the NSE Emerge archive (S1) and on the company's investor site. Every WebFetch of the NSE PDF timed out, the company copy returned only a bot-check page, and direct downloads were not permitted in this environment, so we could not read the primary document directly. Instead we cross-verified the prospectus contents across several independent secondary sources. Multibagg's prospectus analysis (S5) is the most detailed and supplies the revenue mix, concentration, import, RPT, litigation, lock-in and objects-timing data. Market-size figures come from third-party research with different scopes (S16, S17, S21, S22); S21 and S22 come from search-result snippets only. Subscription data are partial midday day-1 snapshots.
